summary: Monica Esposito was a scholar in Sinology and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Paris/Paris Diderot University. She conducted postdoctoral research at Ca' Foscari, the Sorbonne, and Kansai University, and became Associate Professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Horace Hayman Wilson at Oxford. He taught at East India Company College and Cheltenham College before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1860 to 1887.

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach is an Indologist and linguist who studied at FU Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Bonn. She held professorships at the University of Bonn, the University of Cologne, the University of Bamberg, and Heidelberg University (1990–2006).

Monika Zin specializes in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Jagiellonian University and the University of Munich, she taught at Munich and FU Berlin before becoming a project head at the Saxon Academy and honorary professor at Leipzig University.
Moodeen Sheriff was an Indologist who studied at Madras Medical College. He served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied at Tohoku University and under K. R. Norman at Cambridge. He served as associate professor at Sendai National College of Technology and president of Hosen Gakuen College.
Moritz Abraham Stern was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Heidelberg and under Karl Otfried Müller at Göttingen. He served as Extraordinarius at the University of Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

Moriya Okano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Kanto Gakuin University. He has been affiliated with Musashino University and served as director of the Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies.

Moriz Haupt was a German linguist who studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig University. He served as professor at Leipzig University from 1841 to 1851 and later held a professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1853.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler in Vienna and Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at Charles University and the German University in Prague, serving there as extraordinary and a. ö. professor, and taught at Visva-Bharati University.

Morten Schlütter specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and earned his PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein, later holding academic posts at Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, Wisconsin–Madison, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at University College London. He directed the National Museum Wales and the London Museum, and served as Director-General of Archæology in India for the Archaeological Survey of India (1944–1948).
Morton Klass was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his doctoral degree at Columbia University. He later taught at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.
Mother Sayamagyi was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied as a disciple under U Ba Khin and later succeeded him.

Motohiro Yoritomi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He served as professor at Shuchiin University and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Ekyo Ejima, attended the University of Tsukuba, and earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Tsukuba.
Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is an Indologist and philosopher. He taught as a professor at Vidyasagar College and served in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He has held academic posts at Leipzig University and Heidelberg University.

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He has served as Deputy Director of Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums in Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University.

Mumon Yamada was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Shofukuji, president of Hanazono University from 1949 to 1978, and director of the Institute for Zen Studies.
